title: ACRS: Adjacent Computation Resource Sharing among Partitioned GPU Sub-Cores
problem: Modern GPU sub-core partitioning reduces power and area but prevents task distribution across sub-cores; functional units (FUs) frequently stall waiting for results while adjacent sub-cores have unoccupied FUs, wasting compute capacity.
motivation: Sub-core partitioning is ubiquitous for power reduction in GPUs, but this design creates an efficiency ceiling by preventing cross-sub-core resource utilization under workload imbalance.
method: When one sub-core has an instruction stuck waiting for data, ACRS borrows an idle functional unit from an adjacent sub-core to run it instead. The first module (SF_ISSUE) detects stuck instructions and idle neighboring units, then sends the instruction across; the second module (SF_WriteBack) sends the result back. By always targeting the same adjacent sub-core, ACRS avoids expensive rewiring.
key_novelty: ACRS dynamically shares functional units among adjacent sub-cores in partitioned GPUs by offloading instructions waiting for data to idle neighbors.
contributions: Identification of cross-sub-core FU availability during operand collector blockages
Dynamic instruction offloading framework with matching policies
Result routing mechanism with fixed target core to minimize wiring
46.4% maximum performance improvement, 14.1% average, 8.3% energy reduction
primary_theme: Dynamic cross-sub-core functional unit sharing in partitioned GPUs
